title: A Distant Spiral in Virgo
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 5037, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. RosarioAcknowledgement: L. Shatz

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Delicate structures of gas and dust show in fine detail across the spiral galaxy NGC 5037, even though it lies about 150 million light-years from Earth. The galaxy is in the constellation Virgo, and William Herschel first recorded it in 1785.

The detail comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, or WFC3, which gathered the exposures combined into this image. WFC3 is a versatile camera. It can record ultraviolet, visible and infrared light, giving astronomers a wealth of information about whatever it observes.

Astronauts installed WFC3 on Hubble in 2009 during servicing mission 4, the telescope's fifth and final servicing mission. That mission was meant to extend Hubble's life by another five years. When this image was released, 12 years later, both the telescope and the camera were still in active use.
scale: NGC 5037 lies about 150 million light-years from Earth, according to ESA/Hubble.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 observed NGC 5037 in visible light at 606 nm and near-infrared light at 1.6 μm. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of this light is near-infrared, invisible to the eye, and Hubble's sharp view resolves fine gas and dust structures.
